application_review: RoughHorizontalSplitting assembles positive-degree construction from the actual binomial obstruction, constant-term thinning and smooth-step preservation. The initial length L precedes even the filter and scale sequences; the eventual threshold precedes every varying progression, coefficient polynomial, residue and sample step. It returns one common subprogression and all coefficient models with the H-independent original error constant.

RoughScaledMonomials proves exact inverse-scale cancellation, finite monomial product estimates, evaluation of actual multivariate monomials, total-degree reduction under a nonzero coordinate derivative, and bounds for actual MvPolynomial.pderiv monomials.

RoughSlowPolynomial constructs the actual multivariate error polynomial as a constant plus finite monomial sum. It proves whole-box value and algebraic partial-derivative estimates, then bounds them by 1+N*A*C^d and N*d*A*C^d/Z for C>=1 and degree<=d.

RoughModelBoxBounds applies the whole-box estimates to actual differences between real coefficient polynomials and rational coefficient models, using their proved all-index error bounds. It also proves that the assembled error polynomial is exactly the difference of the two finite coefficient polynomials.

Compared with Section 06 coefficient splitting and slow-factor estimates. The assembled theorem chooses L before l,W,S,Z, and one eventual threshold before all changing polynomial coefficients and progression data. It uses the actual displayed weighted obstruction, not assumed rational model existence.

The source length is max(thinning N,2q+2); positive models are restricted to N without changing errors, then one affine subprogression handles the constant term and every positive coefficient. Its step is proved positive and smooth, and every sampled value remains in [S,2S) and coprime to the primorial.
The final common positive coefficient error constant is still roughDescentConstant q card(s) A0 (2^q) q. Neither initial length L nor target H occurs in it. Constant model errors remain in [0,1).

The monomial estimate proves the exact cancellation of Z^(-e) against spatial size Z^e; the partial derivative removes one exponent, leaving one inverse Z. Zero coordinate exponents are handled separately, so natural truncated subtraction cannot silently lower the wrong degree.

The partial derivative is the actual MvPolynomial.pderiv of the constructed polynomial, with its proved monomial coefficient and exponent formula. These are algebraic partial-derivative bounds; no group observable Lipschitz estimate or sampling comparison is assumed or claimed.

The coarse box estimates require C>=1; any fixed positive paper radius may be enlarged to max(1,C). Constants depend on fixed support count, degree, A and box radius, not H, Z or polynomial coefficients. The exact finite-sum estimates retain individual exponents.

The model-to-box interface uses Finsupp multiindices, whereas the earlier extraction interface uses finite functions. Instantiating the finite-function/Finsupp equivalence in a future group-level assembly remains explicit bookkeeping; this batch does not claim that final native group assembly.
All retained proof sources and axiom sets are unchanged; these are author-side checks, not independent kernel replay.
